decisions.source: Owner confirmation

decisions.decision: Enter GridMarket in two tracks: Open Grid Data and Most Commercializable.
decisions.rationale: Fit to the Track is worth 30 points. The explainable prediction built on outage, congestion and price data fits Open Grid Data. A member-facing flexibility market fits Most Commercializable. One demo serves both tracks.
decisions.source: Owner answer to Scope Definition Q1, 2026-09-25 CDT; reference/hackathon-brief.md Tracks and Judging

decisions.decision: The team is the owner plus 1 to 3 human teammates.
decisions.rationale: The team size sets build capacity. Exact headcount was not stated and is deferred (see DEC-GM-016).
decisions.source: Owner answer to Scope Definition Q2, 2026-09-25 CDT

decisions.decision: Build in phases. Every phase must end in a state that can be demoed without crashing. The core is phase 1, and later phases are added in order until the feature freeze at Sun 2026-09-27 07:00 CDT.
decisions.rationale: Owner, verbatim: 'I want to win but also want to complete it'. Phasing protects the 15 Completeness points. The 07:00 freeze leaves time to record the video and 30 minutes of buffer before the 11:00 submission.
decisions.source: Owner answer to Scope Definition Q3, 2026-09-25 CDT

decisions.decision: Phase 2 is a second provider adapter, LoneStar Storage, a simulated second provider company whose customers trade on the same exchange. The remaining phases and stretch items are built at the same time by 2 or 3 parallel Bearing workstreams, and the Integration Engineer assembles their outputs. The integrated branch must always stay demoable.
decisions.rationale: The owner expressed interest in the adapter, and it satisfies success criterion 6 (platform, not a Base-only app). The owner wants parallel workstreams working like a real team. Whether they run as separate Lifecycles or as Coordinator waves is decided in Planning and Design, under the rule of one checkout lease per Lifecycle with approved worktrees.
decisions.source: Owner answer to Scope Definition Q4, 2026-09-25 CDT

decisions.decision: The application and the demo get ERCOT data by live polling of the ERCOT Public API only. The owner registers the ERCOT account and holds the credentials. Credentials are stored locally, untracked, and never committed.
decisions.rationale: The owner declined record-and-replay and replay-only. Discovered API facts: an account, a subscription key and a password-login ID token are required; the token lasts 1 hour and cannot be refreshed; the limit is 30 requests per minute, and exceeding it returns HTTP 429; access is US-only; a request without a key returns 401. Recorded risk: an ERCOT outage, a 429 or a token expiry during the video recording, and no ERCOT data for the workstreams until the owner's key exists.
decisions.source: Owner answer to Scope Definition Q5, 2026-09-25 CDT; developer.ercot.com registration-and-authentication and known-limits pages

decisions.decision: Future contracts settle at expiration against the hourly average of the load zone's ERCOT real-time settlement point price (NP6-905, the four 15-minute intervals) for the delivery hour. The price is converted from $/MWh to $/credit by dividing by 1000, since 1 credit equals 1 kWh. Cash P&L = (reference price - trade price) x quantity.
decisions.rationale: Intent section 7 required a defined reference value but did not define one. This reference comes from real ERCOT data, can be checked independently, and cannot be moved by market participants.
decisions.source: Owner answer to Scope Definition Q6, 2026-09-25 CDT; gridmarket-intent.html section 7

decisions.decision: Host on the spectre-dev workstation, not the Mac mini, which is reserved for azedge. Run inside an isolated VM or container. Expose only through an outbound Cloudflare named tunnel, live from the Sunday demo recording through awards at 15:00 CDT, then take it down. Judges receive rate-limited sandbox API keys.
decisions.rationale: No deploy pipeline is needed, the ERCOT credentials stay on the owner's machine, and the traffic leaves from the US. The owner accepted the public exposure window. The isolation mechanism is decided in Planning and Design. Recorded risk: the workstation is a single point of failure.
decisions.source: Owner answer to Scope Definition Q7, 2026-09-25 CDT

decisions.decision: Stack: Python 3.12 with uv, FastAPI, and a SQLite ledger for the backend; a React and Vite dashboard using Astryx; Docker Compose behind cloudflared. The matching engine sits behind one interface. A Rust (PyO3) matching core is a stretch workstream only, and only with a before-and-after benchmark.
decisions.rationale: The intent's SDK and algorithm examples are in Python. All required tools are already installed on spectre-dev. The limits that matter are ERCOT's 30 requests per minute and the demo load, not raw speed. A Rust core would help the Performance score only if a benchmark proves it.
decisions.source: Owner answer to Scope Definition Q8, 2026-09-25 CDT; spectre-dev installed-tools check

decisions.decision: Use a private repository under the owner's personal GitHub account, not the alphazede org. Teammates are added as collaborators, and main is PR-only. Before submission on Sunday, after a secret scan and a license are in place, the owner makes the repository public. Creating the repository and making it public are owner actions.
decisions.rationale: Teammates and parallel workstreams need a shared remote tonight. Keeping the repository private until the secret scan passes protects the ERCOT credentials and hides unfinished work. Making the repository public is owner-only publication.
decisions.source: Owner answer to Scope Definition Q9, 2026-09-25 CDT

decisions.decision: Phase 1 (the core) contains: ERCOT ingestion of real-time and day-ahead settlement point prices, load forecast, NP3-233 outage capacity and NP6-86 shadow prices and binding constraints; an explainable opportunity score per zone with its drivers; seeded users with $1,000 and simulated batteries; spot and future products on one matching engine; order submission, price-time matching, atomic capacity reservation, ledger and P&L; a REST API with API keys and a Python example; and a live dashboard with seeded bot traffic. Security controls are never cut: atomic capacity reservation, API-key authentication, idempotency keys, maximum order size and rate limits. Stretch items run in parallel: an adversarial scenario with a kill switch, a backtest of the score against real-time prices, and the Rust core. All P2 items are out.
decisions.rationale: Covers the insight and usability scores for both tracks, fits the smallest possible team, and keeps the section 15 security controls.
decisions.source: Owner confirmation of shared understanding, item 1, 2026-09-25 CDT

decisions.decision: Drop the TypeScript trading example.
decisions.rationale: The Python example covers the judge demo (intent section 13, demo step 7).
decisions.source: Owner confirmation of shared understanding, item 2, 2026-09-25 CDT

decisions.decision: Tests may use fixture data. The live-only rule in DEC-GM-007 applies to the application and demo data path.
decisions.rationale: Allows deterministic verification, and allows workstreams to build before the owner's ERCOT key exists, without changing the live-only demo.
decisions.source: Owner confirmation of shared understanding, item 3, 2026-09-25 CDT

decisions.decision: License the public repository under MIT.
decisions.rationale: DEC-GM-011 requires a license before the repository goes public.
decisions.source: Owner confirmation of shared understanding, item 4, 2026-09-25 CDT

decisions.decision: Acceptance: phase 1 passes when success criteria 1 to 5 and 7 to 11 from intent section 22 are all shown in one uninterrupted run through the tunnel URL. Phase 2 adds criterion 6 (multiple provider fleets). Exact headcount and the owner of the demo video are deferred to lane assignment in Planning and Design and must be settled before the Sun 2026-09-27 07:00 CDT freeze.
decisions.rationale: Makes acceptance falsifiable against the intent's success criteria. Headcount no longer affects scope because delivery is phased, and it is needed only to assign lanes.
decisions.source: Owner confirmation of shared understanding, item 5 and the acceptance proposal, 2026-09-25 CDT; gridmarket-intent.html section 22

decisions.decision: Split the owner's new signals. The phase 1 explainable opportunity score adds three normalized, explained drivers: NWS hourly temperature (heat stress), an on-peak/off-peak and NERC holiday flag (5x16 calendar rule: hours ending 07-22 Central Prevailing Time, weekdays, excluding the six NERC holidays; standard library only, no new dependency), and NWS active extreme-weather alerts for Texas (the 'events' signal). A new ML stretch lane (intent P2 item 26) uses all of those signals plus Open-Meteo weather history, Census county population estimates, and LEHD LODES8 Texas workplace (WAC) versus residence (RAC) job counts as a daytime population weight per zone. It is trained on ERCOT archive data and compared against the deterministic score through the stretch backtest. Dropped: a special-events feed and TxDOT traffic data.
decisions.rationale: The owner asked for weather, on-peak/off-peak, events, location and peak-hour population, from free APIs or State of Texas data. These sources were verified without a key (HTTP 200) on 2026-09-25: NWS api.weather.gov hourly forecast and /alerts/active?area=TX; the Open-Meteo forecast and archive; the Census county population estimates CSV; and the LODES8 Texas WAC files for 2021 and 2022. The phase 1 signals are live, need no key, fit the live-only rule in DEC-GM-007, and work before the owner's ERCOT key exists. The static population weights only become meaningful once they are fitted against history, so they belong in the ML lane. Training on historical archives is offline model work, not the application or demo data path, so it does not conflict with DEC-GM-007 or DEC-GM-014. Location was already decided through load zones (DEC-GM-012). Special events were dropped because the Austin, Houston and data.texas.gov endpoints return 200 but hold only stale or regulatory data. TxDOT was dropped because it publishes annual average daily traffic only, with no hourly counts. The keyless Open-Meteo fetcher in alphazede/alphazede-sports at cd3dbaf (services/data_node/fetchers/weather_fetcher.py and fetchers/data_signals.py) may be ported. The OpenWeatherMap client and its OPENWEATHER_API_KEY are not needed. Checks left for Planning and Design: the Open-Meteo free-tier terms for a public repository; the LODES8 RAC file path (same pattern as WAC, not probed); and the Texas Demographic Center direct CSV, which returned 404 and is covered by the Census file instead.
decisions.source: Owner answers to Scope Definition Q11, 2026-09-25 CDT (verbatim: 'For the ML algorithm we should add weather, on-peak off-peak, events, location, population during peak hours'; 'so we need to get apis for weather I have one in alphazedsports in the gh repo. and other free apis or state of texas data'; answer: Split); keyless source probes 2026-09-25

decisions.decision: DEC-GM-012's rule that all P2 items are out no longer applies to intent P2 item 26 (the ML prediction model). Item 26 is now an ML stretch lane that runs in parallel with the other stretch items and follows DEC-GM-017. The phase 1 core list stays as it was, except that three drivers are added to the opportunity score: NWS temperature, the peak/holiday flag and NWS alerts. All other P2 items remain out.
decisions.rationale: The owner's new ML signal intent reopened item 26. Under DEC-GM-005 and DEC-GM-006, stretch lanes must never block a demoable, non-crashing phase 1.

decisions.decision: The owner created the private repository https://github.com/1wgrumph/gridmarket under their personal account and seeded main. GitHub refused a PR-only ruleset on a free private repository with HTTP 403. Until the owner makes the repository public on Sunday, PR-only main is a working convention that all humans and agents must follow. The owner applies the ruleset after the repository is public.
decisions.rationale: Records the realized state of DEC-GM-011 and the enforcement gap before the public flip. Pushing directly to main is prohibited by convention even though GitHub does not yet enforce it. The public flip remains an owner action, gated on the secret scan and the MIT license (DEC-GM-011, DEC-GM-015).
decisions.source: Owner action relayed by the Orchestrator, 2026-09-25 CDT; GitHub ruleset API response HTTP 403
Owner in chat, verbatim: 'you can just build the spec its part of the presentation I want to show the judges. add it part of the plan if you half too'
decisions.decision: Add a Spec lane to the GridMarket plan. It builds (1) the spec template: generated front matter plus the outline, per-section pattern (BLUF; Frame of Who/What/Why/How/When/Where; prose with no word limit; one table or figure when the structural trigger fires; at most 5 requirements per section, bound per feature), 8 table classes T1-T8 and 8 figure classes F1-F8; (2) azdiagram, a Python generator using Graphviz layout for graph classes, draw.io output from Graphviz coordinates, a grid renderer for sequence and timing, and overlap/size lint; (3) the spec-author, spec-diagram and spec-lint skills; (4) GridMarket's own specification written in that template with its figures. The GridMarket specification is a product deliverable in the gridmarket repo, shown to the judges in the demo and presentation. It is outside Bearing's five planning artifacts and requires no bearing-lite change. The lane runs in parallel and must not block the phase 1 demo.
decisions.inputs: AZHQ journey HQ-SPEC-2026-09-25 decisions DEC-SPEC-004 through DEC-SPEC-007 and DEC-SPEC-010 (outline, section pattern, classes, tooling). Graphviz 2.42.2 and draw.io 31.5.2 are installed on spectre-dev.

decisions.source: Kickoff deck slide 17 and slide 11, transcribed in reference/hackathon-brief.md
decisions.decision: Hackathon rule: all code required for the submission to run is written during the hackathon; open source code is allowed only if it has been open source for at least 2 weeks. Therefore the private alphazede-sports Open-Meteo fetcher is NOT ported; the weather client is written fresh (DEC-GM-017 port note superseded). Submission needs a GitHub link, project description, and a 3-5 minute MAX Loom video; submitting takes 15-20 minutes. Max team size 5.
